text:
jordana: Quick report — sampleapp batch helper sent 512-dim vectors to /rerank and the service rejected them. Getting a dimension mismatch error from the reranker.

mike: Copy logs? curious if client did any auto-pad/trim or if model metadata is wrong. :grimacing: 

jordana: Redacted POST: {requests:[{id:q1, text:"...", embedding:[0.12,0.03,.../*512 vals*/]}], model:"open-embed-xl-512"}
Server 400: "vector length 512 != expected 768 for model open-embed-xl-768"

sam: Sounds like a config drift between the sampleapp and the rerank pipeline. Two ideas: helper selected a quantized 512 fallback, or an SDK layer changed the vector shape.

lina: Also noticed cross-language parity: Go & Node SDKs silently pad to 768, Python errors. That inconsistency hides problems for some users and surfaces for others.

mike: Actionable short-term: make the batch helper validate dims locally before sending. Either reject with a clear message or support an explicit pad/trim mode.

jordana: Proposed client check (pseudo):
```python
expected = model_meta.get('embedding_dim')
for v in batch:
    if len(v) != expected:
        raise ValueError(f"embedding length {len(v)} != expected {expected}. set pad_mode='pad' to auto-pad")
```
Also include an opt-in pad_mode and explicit warning when auto-converting.

sam: Backend suggestion: accept optional header X-Embedding-Dim: 512 so the server can route to a compatible reranker or return a clear, actionable error listing the expected dim and candidate models.

lina: There's a retry/auth edge: our retrier retried whole batches on timeouts without Idempotency-Key and the reranker applied scores twice. For scoring flows that's terrible. We should add Idempotency-Key by default on batch endpoints and have server ignore exact-duplicate payloads within a short window.

mike: Agreed. Full parity plan: (1) ensure model.metadata.embedding_dim surfaced identically in all SDKs, (2) batch helper validates dims and only pads/trims when explicitly enabled, (3) SDKs add Idempotency-Key header on batch sends, (4) server errors include expected_dim and suggested remediation text.

jordana: I'll open a small PR implementing the dim-check + client-side friendly error mapping. I'll also add a sampleapp integration test that simulates a mismatched-dim request and asserts a clear error.

lina: I'll add the test and a short onboarding note in sampleapp/README: "Confirm model.embedding_dim matches your sampleapp config. If using quantized variants, set pad_mode and include X-Embedding-Dim header." Plus a curl snippet.

mike: Micro-DX item: response field name divergence. Some SDKs return `vector`, some `embedding`, others `embeddings`. Recommend standardizing to `embedding` for single and `embeddings` for batch responses in the public SDKs and adding a thin compatibility shim in sampleapp for legacy names.

sam: Nice. Also suggest server include a human-friendly error example: e.g., {error: "dim_mismatch", expected_dim: 768, got: 512, help: "use model X or set pad_mode"} so SDKs can map to better exceptions.

devx-bot: Created task DEVEX-3160: "embed batch helper: dim validation + pad_mode + idempotency" and linked this thread.

jordana: Thanks. I'll add the compatibility shim and opt-in pad_mode in the PR.

mike: Also add docs page under devex for "Embedding dims and rerank compatibility" with examples in curl, Python, and Node.

lina: Will draft the README blurb and tests, will ping when ready. :thumbsup: 

jordana: Resolved for now; follow-ups tracked in DEVEX-3160.

mike: Thanks team! :rocket:
